title: Changes in Conditions
paragraphs: Ren and Itsuki aren’t here—there’s a different group instead. They’re all armed and taking aim at us.
“See? Just as I thought. These guys are all idiots.”

Takt is being unusually provocative. But since I’ve taken him down countless times before, I feel nothing but cool detachment. Specifically, it’s something along the lines of, “Since they’ve come out here so brazenly, I might as well kill them.”
“They’re supposed to be summoned when a wave hits, but they were hiding like idiots.”

Oh my, it seems they think we accidentally appeared in the wave. How foolish. We only joined because there were people in trouble from the wave. Above all, if Ren and Itsuki die, we’ll get stuck in a loop.
“Seriously, it’s a pain that all my enemies are nothing but Trash and idiots.”

It seems Takt really does think that. Well, enemies generally tend to look like fools. Before I realized true love, I, in my foolishness, thought Father was a complete idiot. For a hero, he buys slaves, goes peddling without even leveling up—it all seemed like nothing but a waste of time. It was the same when I looked at Ren and Itsuki; I secretly looked down on them, thinking they lacked even a shred of efficiency or rationality.

I’m sure, from Takt’s perspective, I must have looked like just another fool who fell into the trap I’d set myself. Back in middle and high school, whenever I defeated an opponent through strategy, I used to think, “How utterly stupid to fall for something so simple.”

But looking back now, that’s nothing more than hindsight. After all, if I’d lost back then, it would have meant I was the fool. To put it bluntly, the winner is smart, and the loser is a fool. No matter how much strategy the loser employs, they’ll just be labeled a fool pretending to be smart.
But in reality, that’s not the case. Every living being is constantly searching for the best move they can conceive.

There may be failures along the way. There may be mistakes. But no one acts with the intention of bringing misfortune upon themselves. That goes for me, Father, Filo-chan, and my older sister—and even Ren and Itsuki, who aren’t here right now.
But pigs, Takt, and reincarnated people are a different story. Those guys are fighting just to make themselves miserable.
…By the way, why aren’t Ren and Itsuki here?
“That’s strange, isn’t it? Where are Ren and Itsuki?”

I couldn’t care less about Takt, who’s getting a little too cocky right now. No matter how much I look around, Ren and Itsuki aren’t here. In almost every loop, Ren and Itsuki were supposed to be here… so what’s going on here?

Sensing something ominous, not only Big Sisters but also the villagers are maintaining a state of readiness. Rescue was supposed to be the priority, but things have taken a different turn. Father turns his gaze toward me while holding his shield in front of him.
“Motoyasu, weren’t you supposed to meet Ren and Itsuki here?”
“I thought so, but…”

How on earth did I end up running into Takt in a place like this? Well, I had planned to deal with him once the Queen returned, crushed the Three Heroes Sect, proved Father’s innocence, and began developing my Older Sister’s village—but this is the first time I’ve ever seen him here. Takt seems to be in a good mood, doesn’t he? He’s giving me a creepy look. That face of his still makes me want to puke.
“Ah, you guys look like you don’t know who I am.”
“Not at all. You’re not welcome here.”

Takt looks a bit put out by my words, but it’s not like he doesn’t know who I am. He’s one of the top three scumbags on my “must-kill” list, after all. Number one is Crimson Swine, number two is Takt, and number three is Dragon.
Takt’s sporting some kind of smarmy, creepy grin. Should I just make him vanish right now? Just as I’m thinking that, Father stops me, so I’ll have to hold back just a little longer.
“So? Motoyasu. Who’s this guy waiting outside?”
Father asked me that. But perhaps in response to those words, Takt started talking.
“It’s a pleasure to meet you for the first time. It would be a pity for me to be killed by some nameless guy like this, and the women around here should know the name of the true hero.”
“Wait, I wasn’t asking you…”
Just as Father said, he’s not worth listening to at all. My inner voice is whispering that it’s fine to just vaporize him without a second thought.
“My name is Takt Alsaholn Faubrey. I am the Seven-Star Hero and Savior who will send you otherworlders—who’ve been getting too cocky and doing as you please—to the afterlife!”
As he said that, Takt swung down—not his claws, but his sword.
“Starkfaar!”
With a loud crack, the ground split open right at my feet, and something began gushing out.
“Motoyasu!”
“Yes!”

It looked like something was about to burst out of the crack, so I slammed my spear into it and then smashed it to pieces with an Air Strike Javelin. That was a pretty flimsy attack. Takt’s attack crumbled easily.
“What!? …Hmph. Looks like a weaker skill than I thought.”
“What the hell are you doing all of a sudden?!”

Father glares at Takt, radiating killing intent. A sneak attack… still a pointless strategy, as always. He must have targeted me because he underestimated me as the Shield Hero, thinking Father-in-law couldn’t attack me.
“It’s just my way of saying hello, isn’t it?”

Just how shameless can he be? I think it’s about time I killed him on the spot, but I’m holding back because Father is stopping me. If he so much as hurts little Filo, I’ll shake off Father’s restraint and kill him in the most gruesome way possible.
“Hey, if you don’t cut it out, my mad dog’s going to do something so terrible it’d be better if he were dead.”

Father glares at Takt with eyes that send chills down my spine—eyes filled with even more murderous intent. Lately, Father has been using the term “mad dog” a lot, but isn’t he expecting a little too much from Keel? I’ll take him out in a flash—no need to even wait for Keel to show up.
“Ha… well, fine. It wouldn’t be any fun otherwise.”
“I couldn’t care less about what you find fun. But… that sword and those Skills…”
As Father stares intently at the sword Takt is holding, Takt looks down on us with the expression of a child who’s just gotten a new toy.
“Ah, don’t you get it?”
As if to say, “Figure it out,” Takt proudly flaunts his sword. Immediately, the Pope of the Three Heroes Sect—who was standing there proudly holding a replica weapon—spoke to Takt.
“This is marvelous. A true child of God is here in this very place—one capable of reclaiming the sacred weapon from the false hero who desecrated our faith, and wielding it…”
“I’ve got all kinds of weapons, but when it comes down to it, a sword is the real deal. It’s like it was made just for me. Listen up—I’m going to make sure you all understand that.”
What’s that supposed to mean? I’m not sure why, but I’ve got a really bad feeling about this. Yeah… it’s that feeling that something I’ve always taken for granted has suddenly changed.

“Since I’m the one who can save the world, I’ll take both the Seven Star Weapons and the Holy Weapons… No, that’s not quite right. I’m merely selecting temporary owners so they’ll eventually end up in my hands. So when I encounter the rightful owner, the weapon will end up in that person’s… my hands.”

…What on earth is this guy talking about? Some guy like Takt is the rightful owner? Your abilities are nothing more than a slightly upgraded version of a common thief’s. You’re only good for cleaning up that annoying army of reincarnated folks, yet you’re acting way too high and mighty for no reason.
“Judging by the way you put it… you took it from Ren?”
“He isn’t the Sword Hero. It was just an imposter wielding the real Holy Weapon.”
“Huh? You didn’t actually think the Sword Hero was the only one, did you?”
As if to show off, Takt sheathes his sword and summons a bow. Could it be that even Itsuki had his weapon taken from him?
“Man, that was hilarious. Even though it just ended up in the rightful owner’s hands, those guys were screaming for it back. I taught them the hard way who the rightful owner really is.”
“So you killed them… Ren and Itsuki?”
Takt didn’t deny it; he just wore a proud expression. …Ren and Itsuki are dead? Then why isn’t the loop repeating?
“Motoyasu, if what he says is true, it looks like the conditions have changed.”
Father said in a low voice. A change in conditions. This is exactly what Father was worried about right when we first entered this loop.
“If you don’t want to die, hand over the weapon to me—its rightful owner—right this instant.”
“Don’t be ridiculous.”

Father replied in an annoyed tone. I’m ready to fight at any moment! We should cut this preamble short and kill him right away. But Father is holding up his hand as if to say he won’t allow it just yet. Presumably, it’s to draw information out of Takt.
“Well, I’ve answered your question. If you want to live even a little longer, just confess honestly.”
“Confess, huh. Unfortunately, unlike Ren and Itsuki, I’m not very familiar with this world.”
“It’s no use hiding it! Where did you take Malty, the princess of this country?!”
Saying that, Takt pointed at me and Father. ……Malty? I feel like I’ve heard that name somewhere before, but who was she again? Oh, you mean the Crimson Swine?
As I was thinking that, Father gave me a silent look. Well, I guess I have no choice.
“Crimson Swine, is it? That guy isn’t in this world anymore. Hahahahahaha!”
“Wh—you bastard! Don’t you dare joke around like that!”
Takt’s face turned bright red as he yelled at the top of his lungs. It’s not like I was joking—I was just stating the facts, wasn’t I?
“This is no joke. I’m the one who wiped that guy off the face of the earth.”
“Don’t mess with me! Do you really think something like that’s allowed?!”
“It’s not a matter of whether it’s allowed or not. That guy was a menace. Compared to his actions, the misdeeds Ren and Itsuki committed are trivial.”
Takt must have been furious at my reply, because his eyes narrowed, he clenched his teeth, and then he shouted.
“Everyone! We’re going to weaken him to make him spill the real information!”
Oh? Feeling motivated, are you? I, for one, couldn’t wait to finish him off.
“I’ve already conquered this world! We don’t need you ‘people from another world’ here! Just hand over your weapons, spill the information, and get lost!”
HAHAHA. “Conquered”… Takt sure has a way with jokes. And speaking of “people from another world,” aren’t you one yourself?
“Fire!”
With that, he tried to unleash his usual, one-trick-pony All Cannon Fire right at us.
“Shooting Star Shield X! Air Strike Shield X! Second Shield X! You guys! Hide behind me!”
“Yes, sir!”
“What the hell is this!?”
“Boo.”

Starting with Filo-tan, the girls line up behind Father in sync with Takt’s attacks. Immediately afterward, Takt’s All Cannon Fire is fired. The bullets fly off in a whirlwind, but they merely produce a faint spark before being deflected by the shields and barriers Father has raised.
“Motoyasu, you get behind me too—”
I anticipate the bullets’ trajectory and dodge them with the bare minimum of movement. The attack is so slow it makes me yawn. And finally, I dodged it with a graceful backward bridge.
Father stares at me with a blank expression.
“That’s disgusting!”

Filo-chan spat out, glaring at Takt! That’s right. Takt is certainly a repulsive creature! For the sake of Filo-chan’s mental stability, we should dispose of him as soon as possible. Snapping back to my original stance, I turned to face Father, hoping to get his permission.
“Wha… You’re just standing there, completely unfazed after taking All Cannon Fire from my companions, who are all at least Lv. 250!?”
“Nonsense… Could the Demon of the Shield and that impostor Spear Hero really possess such power?”
Takt, the Pope of the Three Heroes Sect, and that bunch of pigs are all letting out cries of shock. A puny little shot like that wouldn’t even hurt if it hit me.
“You’d think you’d figure it out just by seeing Motoyasu casually deflect those Skills meant as a greeting.”
That’s right. It’s obvious at a glance that Takt was just testing out a new skill and discarded it as weak. That’s just Takt for you.

“Well then, do you understand the difference in our abilities now? Let’s get back to the conversation. Why are you even here? Depending on the situation, I might tell you the real whereabouts of that Bitch of a princess. In a low voice, Father explained why he’d asked Takt such a thing. He said it might be a plot point we’d need to watch out for in case we ever end up in a loop again. Indeed, it certainly wouldn’t hurt to know why Takt appears in the waves of Melromarc.
“You coward!”
“Hah… Say whatever you want. So? What’s the deal?”

“D-damn it… It’s obvious, isn’t it! There was a notice from the Adventurers’ Guild, issued by Melromarc, asking for contact with Myne!”　That’s why we figured Malty must have gotten caught up in some kind of incident, so we came to check on her!”

What?! Could it be that the missing person report actually lured Takt here? That Crimson Swine… whether he’s alive or dead, he’s nothing but trouble—alive, he causes trouble; dead, he brings this kind of disaster! Just how much longer does he intend to hold us back before he’s satisfied?!
“Well, at least we got to punish those overconfident heroes along the way—that’s a big win.”
I think you’re the one getting a big head here, don’t you? Anyway… my patience is about to run out. Father must have sensed this too, because he lowered his hand, which had been holding me back.
